reasons.A: Mixes short, flat declaratives with long balanced sentences the way the passage does, ends each part on an aphorism ('The wanderer makes the road; the citizen walks upon it'), and uses Victorian diction and dashes without overdoing them; it only lacks the passage's exclamations and first person.
reasons.B: Gets the passage's exclamatory, first-person, argumentative stance and period feel, but its sentences are mostly long semicolon chains without the passage's short punches, and 'verily' and 'nay' lay the archaism on thicker than the passage does.
reasons.C: Modern, hedged, even-tempered prose ('I am not so sure', 'It helps to remember') with plain contemporary diction and no period rhythm, exclamation or rhetorical flourish; the furthest from the author's voice.
